title: The Gargantuan Lie That is Collapsing The World’s Climate
excerpt: Thinking we have time left to address climate change, or that “Net Zero by 2050” will save us, is driving us toward full social collapse in ways that become more obvious with every new broken temperature record.
content_html:
Lies are a lot like gourds. They come in hundreds of different varieties, sizes, and bulbous, twisty shapes. Some are off-puttingly spiked and prickly, while others remind us of fall childhood memories.

Some lies, if prepared correctly like squash or pumpkin, can appear delicious and irresistible, concealing a dark reality: “I can’t believe you’re not a model! For five thousand dollars I can photograph you so you have a portfolio.” The central aim of most lies is to avoid consequences. When an untruth is especially desperate and self-serving, it can be unintentionally hilarious: "Yes I tried marijuana... but I did not inhale.” 

Embezzling money or murdering someone for the insurance pay-out are part of a phylum of lies that cross into serious criminality. These deceptions’ sphere of influence often stays fairly localized. But sometimes covering up the initial lie can spawn lots of other lies that spread and spread, like with Watergate or Bernie Madoff. What started as a little decorative Thanksgiving-gourd-sized lie suddenly becomes larger and quite ugly. This family of lies strives to not only avoid consequences, but to gain status and resources, another common end game of many deceptions. And then there are the large society-wide lies: hulking distortions and misrepresentations watered and tended to by leaders, mass media, culture, and industry.

This particular sub-genus of grifts, half-truths and strategic omissions have led throughout modern history to wars, mass death, societal collapse, and the theft of humanity’s great treasures. “Manifest Destiny.” “Aryan superiority.” “The divine right of kings.” “The domino theory.” “Israel has a right to defend itself.” “Oxycontin isn’t addictive because it’s time-released.” These county-fair, blue ribbon-winning prevarications tend to be driven by a myriad of short-term incentives, irrational manipulated fears, unexamined assumptions, convenient blind spots, and of course… the desire to avoid consequences and expand status and resources.

“People always pay their mortgages” became the half-true rallying cry used by Wall Street, news media, and politicians to collapse the world economy in 2007. Turns out when you change lending rules to feed an unregulated derivatives market by giving mortgages to people who can’t pay them… they don’t. “Saddam Hussein has weapons of mass destruction” (along with the subvariations on the central lie—“We want to bring democracy,” “If you don’t support the troops, you support the terrorists,” “Saddam orchestrated 9/11,” etc) killed a million people, devastated the entire nation of Iraq, and in many ways also gutted the United States, all while enriching oil companies, weapons manufacturers, big banks, juicing TV ratings, and expanding the power of the Bush/Cheney presidency.

However, there is one type of rare, gargantuan, towering lie that makes all the other mass lies throughout human history seem like frightened, scurrying, little adorable fibs.

It is a lie told worldwide by hundreds of thousands of institutions, elected officials, many universities, legacy news, some large non-profits and eventually—as the deception entered mainstream culture—even by ourselves, to ourselves, every single moment of every day. It is a constantly growing gourd that even as a baby back in the 1970s was the size of three aircraft carriers. These days it is so massive it is almost easier to refer to what isn’t part of it (Disneyland, a BLT, that green croc by the side of the highway) than what is.

This massive lie can best be summed up as “when it comes to climate change... we have more time.”

To be clear, we are not talking about the kind of total climate denial one would find on the extremist, lunatic fringe inhabited by the likes of Alex Jones or the current U.S. President. And we’re not referring to cartoonish hucksters and “climate skeptics” like Joe Rogan or Jordan Peterson.

Polling shows only 14.8 percent of Americans deny the basic sixth grade science behind global warming. To put that in perspective, as much as 10 percent of the population still believes the Earth is flat.

No, the monstrous, misshapen garden colossus lie we’re referring to is subscribed to by most of the U.S., has stopped and slowed climate action far more than outright denial, and keeps growing and growing. Every day this deception whispers seductively in the ears of mankind: “global warming is real but not urgent… Keep doing what you’re doing.”

Less embarrassing than “climate change is a Chinese hoax,” but every bit as unscientific and ridiculous, it is the preferred lie of the ruling class, mainstream news media, and corporations.

Sir David King—former science advisor to the United Kingdom, professor at Oxford and then Cambridge, winner of too many awards to list and as establishment as they come—was quoted as saying that what we do over the next three to four years will determine the fate of humankind.

He said this... in 2021.

Like all grand lies, “we have more time” takes many different forms, often focus-grouped. There are the lofty-sounding promises to reach “Net-zero emissions by 2050,” as if 24 years from now was soon enough. There are the queries of “What’s your carbon footprint?,” as if individual people with plastic bags or straws were the problem and not gigantic multinational corporations. There’s the accusation that anyone who expresses urgency is a “doomer.” There are those who treat climate as an abstraction to win political campaigns, first arguing that the Biden administration’s Inflation Reduction Act was a victory despite doing nowhere near enough to address the scale of climate collapse, and more recently that Democrats should just stop talking about climate and focus on more “winnable” issues. Most damaging and common of all, there are those who simply don’t mention it.

All of these distortions have robbed us of the most critical element people need to understand a threat and adjust their actions accordingly: context.

And make no mistake, when it comes to how much time we have, the data and the geological record are crystal clear.

For some badly-needed context, the last three years, likely for the first time in over 100,000 years, have averaged above the Paris Accords’ “do not cross” 1.5 degrees celsius planetary warming. Only ten years ago, that was considered catastrophic, but now mainstream news tells us it’s just a number.

And with a bump coming next year from a growing, historic El Niño up to 1.7 degrees celsius average warming, likely to cause agricultural failure and food shortages, we are staring right at the vaunted 2C number.

Why is 2C so vaunted?

Let’s do the context thing again: 2C will mean we have completely left the stable climate period known as the Holocene. This is the 11,000-year-old era that has given us large-scale crop and livestock agriculture, which gave us cities, written language, modern science and medicine, and warm beds and showers.

Before that, for hundreds of thousands of years in the Pleistocene era, humans (and our hominid ancestors) spent most of their time running from drought, fires, floods, extreme cold and heat, predators, and each other.

The population was likely no more than a few million people spread across the whole planet. At one point we may have almost gone extinct, with just 10,000 Homo sapiens clinging to life. But after the advent of the Holocene and its remarkably stable climate, in only 100 centuries the world population has risen to 8 billion.

That is what we stand to lose. In fact, if our institutions, news and elected officials continue to feed and water the oil company-conceived mega-falsehood that climate breakdown is something just “our great-grandkids need to worry about,”  human civilization as we know it will collapse and billions could die. And we’re not talking about the far distant future. We are talking about collapse within years, not centuries. For real.

This is right around the corner. A joint study by the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries and the University of Exeter suggests that a 2C temperature increase by 2050—which we are hurtling towards, with no plans of slowing down—could result in two billion deaths. And that is virtually the best-case scenario, as temperature rise predictions have worsened and put 1.5C of warming out of reach. According to the United Nations, in order to limit warming to 2C, we would need “emissions to drop around 35 per cent by 2035.” Even if “current national commitments” were fully implemented they “would cut emissions only 12 to 15 per cent by that date.”

The other scenario, which scientists now say “recent data aligns more closely with,” is 3C of warming. At that level, the Exeter authors warn of up to 4 billion deaths. Four billion. That is half the planet. In 26 years or less. Even for those lucky enough to survive the worst weather events, life as we know it would cease to exist due to war, involuntary mass migration, and “catastrophic mortality events from disease, malnutrition, thirst and conflict.” According to the lead author of the report, there is no realistic plan in place to avoid this scenario.

How effective and finely tuned is this civilization-killing lie? Recently, out of curiosity, I asked the people at my nonprofit media studio, Yellow Dot, to create a graph with two data points: mentions of climate on U.S. broadcast news and recent spiking global warming numbers. And this is what they sent me:

One look at the near perfect correlatory X at the center of this graph, and it is clear something about humankind and western civilization is profoundly and deeply broken. The revelation hit me as almost biological in its clarity: as a species, we are behaving like a pod of dolphins beaching themselves because some kind of brain parasite disrupted their echolocation. Our ability to share knowledge and understand the situation we’re in has become utterly compromised, and deadly.

If so many people weren’t dying and going to die, it would almost be impressive. The lie and the financial markets, corporations, and billionaires that suckle on it have created a vast, highly sensitive information system over the decades, consisting of careerists, company men, and people who fear for their jobs. That system has so internalized big capital’s desires that it nearly instantly responds to any threat to big capital’s hegemony. And remember, by “threats” we are referring to the reality of billions of deaths.

Lately, as extreme weather goes into uncharted territory, broadcast and much of online and print news has increasingly been framing each freakish weather disaster as a one-off event disconnected from one of the fastest and most deadly shifts in Earth's history.

For example, take this clip from an NBC news report two weeks ago, about tornadoes striking New York City. It’s remarkable for how it paints a picture of the scale of the crisis we’re facing, without ever mentioning what the crisis is. And there are thousands of news pieces just like it:

Pieces like this put millions of people in active danger by robbing them of the key information they need to adjust their personal risk assessment. Namely, that because oil companies are flooding the planet with heat trapping gases, our environment is getting more and more dangerous every day.

The most recent study of the earth energy imbalance or EEI—the difference between the heat the Earth absorbs from the Sun, and the amount it sends back out into space—shows 12 Hiroshima bombs of heat being trapped by greenhouse gases every single second of every day. As recently as 2020, it was only 5 or 6 atomic bombs’ worth. That’s how fast the crisis is accelerating, but you’d never know it by watching the TV news.

It’s one thing to warn your teen daughter who is going into the city for the weekend not to take a ride from a stranger, and entirely another to fail to mention that the city she’s going to is hosting a serial killer convention.

At this exact moment, oceans are hotter than they’ve ever been since record-keeping began, and air temperatures on average are warmer than they’ve been in around 100,000 years. We refer to humans of the Pleistocene as Hunter Gatherers and not farmers, fishermen, influencers or IT consultants for a reason. Good luck taking corn to market in 135 degree Fahrenheit heat while dodging dry lightning with a saber-toothed tiger stalking you.

Back in 2015, the number chosen for preserving the Holocene and avoiding at least a billion people starving, dying in extreme heat, or in storms or fires was set at 1.5 degrees Celsius, through a mixture of science and political considerations, formalized in the Paris Climate Accord.

We are, once again for the people in the back, averaging over that number for the past three years. And never mind that several renowned scientists, like Michael Mann, think even 1.2C of warming should have been a do-not-cross line.

Still have doubts? If you do, I don’t blame you. We live in a consumer culture hammering us daily with triggering political proclamations, sales pitches, and clickbait designed to spike engagement responses in the brain. “Immigrants are coming for your way of life!” “This new SUV is the best ever!” “Great White Shark Eats Porn Star!” Most of it is misleading, in one way or another, so there’s a natural tendency to assume that “Planet about to boil!” might be too.

But Big Oil and its PR agencies know this, and they’ve weaponized the healthy skepticism we’ve developed as a survival mechanism against those voices speaking the truth about the urgent state of the climate.

After all, who are you going to believe? The New York Times, an outlet famous for downplaying climate urgency, or some weird scientist saying crazy things? Even when a profession famous for dead-eyed, bottom-line risk assessment like insurance actuaries releases a statement about how serious the situation is, corporate news media turns it into what people used to call a “below the fold story,” framing it as just another minor environmental item—not headline news.

In service of the Great Lie, the government of the United Kingdom even tried to bury a climate report from its own intelligence agency before it was leaked. To my knowledge there aren’t many spies being called tree huggers, unless they’re undercover of course. But the MI5 and MI6 are clear-eyed about the danger that’s coming. The report warned that “global ecosystem degradation and collapse threaten UK national security and prosperity.”

No one wants to eat a raw pumpkin. It looks like a Dr. Seuss character’s brain, is full of seeds, and has no real taste. But like with any good lie, when the right sugar, spices, a buttery crust, and time in the oven is added, pumpkin pie becomes a cherished classic.

The same thing happens with the climate lie. The financial markets, massive oil companies, the banks that finance them, the travel industry, car companies, your career and job security, the people you’re having dinner with who don’t want to be bummed out, all of these incentives and forces don’t want you to know you are eating a big, weird gourd.

And as long as we go with their mendacious flow, hundreds of millions, and then billions will die well before “Net Zero by 2050” or “our great grandkids’ future” arrive. Because we are out of time. And we need to get to work immediately. There are a million things to do.

Adam McKay is the Academy Award-winning director of The Big Short, Vice, and Don’t Look Up and the founder of Yellow Dot Studios.

To be clear, we are not talking about the kind of total climate denial one would find on the extremist, lunatic fringe inhabited by the likes of Alex Jones or the current U.S. President. And we’re not referring to cartoonish hucksters and “climate skeptics” like Joe Rogan or Jordan Peterson.

Polling shows only 14.8 percent of Americans deny the basic sixth grade science behind global warming. To put that in perspective, as much as 10 percent of the population still believes the Earth is flat.

No, the monstrous, misshapen garden colossus lie we’re referring to is subscribed to by most of the U.S., has stopped and slowed climate action far more than outright denial, and keeps growing and growing. Every day this deception whispers seductively in the ears of mankind: “global warming is real but not urgent… Keep doing what you’re doing.”

Less embarrassing than “climate change is a Chinese hoax,” but every bit as unscientific and ridiculous, it is the preferred lie of the ruling class, mainstream news media, and corporations.

Sir David King—former science advisor to the United Kingdom, professor at Oxford and then Cambridge, winner of too many awards to list and as establishment as they come—was quoted as saying that what we do over the next three to four years will determine the fate of humankind.

He said this... in 2021.

Like all grand lies, “we have more time” takes many different forms, often focus-grouped. There are the lofty-sounding promises to reach “Net-zero emissions by 2050,” as if 24 years from now was soon enough. There are the queries of “What’s your carbon footprint?,” as if individual people with plastic bags or straws were the problem and not gigantic multinational corporations. There’s the accusation that anyone who expresses urgency is a “doomer.” There are those who treat climate as an abstraction to win political campaigns, first arguing that the Biden administration’s Inflation Reduction Act was a victory despite doing nowhere near enough to address the scale of climate collapse, and more recently that Democrats should just stop talking about climate and focus on more “winnable” issues. Most damaging and common of all, there are those who simply don’t mention it.

All of these distortions have robbed us of the most critical element people need to understand a threat and adjust their actions accordingly: context.

And make no mistake, when it comes to how much time we have, the data and the geological record are crystal clear.

For some badly-needed context, the last three years, likely for the first time in over 100,000 years, have averaged above the Paris Accords’ “do not cross” 1.5 degrees celsius planetary warming. Only ten years ago, that was considered catastrophic, but now mainstream news tells us it’s just a number.

And with a bump coming next year from a growing, historic El Niño up to 1.7 degrees celsius average warming, likely to cause agricultural failure and food shortages, we are staring right at the vaunted 2C number.

Why is 2C so vaunted?

Let’s do the context thing again: 2C will mean we have completely left the stable climate period known as the Holocene. This is the 11,000-year-old era that has given us large-scale crop and livestock agriculture, which gave us cities, written language, modern science and medicine, and warm beds and showers.

Before that, for hundreds of thousands of years in the Pleistocene era, humans (and our hominid ancestors) spent most of their time running from drought, fires, floods, extreme cold and heat, predators, and each other.

The population was likely no more than a few million people spread across the whole planet. At one point we may have almost gone extinct, with just 10,000 Homo sapiens clinging to life. But after the advent of the Holocene and its remarkably stable climate, in only 100 centuries the world population has risen to 8 billion.

That is what we stand to lose. In fact, if our institutions, news and elected officials continue to feed and water the oil company-conceived mega-falsehood that climate breakdown is something just “our great-grandkids need to worry about,”  human civilization as we know it will collapse and billions could die. And we’re not talking about the far distant future. We are talking about collapse within years, not centuries. For real.

This is right around the corner. A joint study by the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries and the University of Exeter suggests that a 2C temperature increase by 2050—which we are hurtling towards, with no plans of slowing down—could result in two billion deaths. And that is virtually the best-case scenario, as temperature rise predictions have worsened and put 1.5C of warming out of reach. According to the United Nations, in order to limit warming to 2C, we would need “emissions to drop around 35 per cent by 2035.” Even if “current national commitments” were fully implemented they “would cut emissions only 12 to 15 per cent by that date.”

The other scenario, which scientists now say “recent data aligns more closely with,” is 3C of warming. At that level, the Exeter authors warn of up to 4 billion deaths. Four billion. That is half the planet. In 26 years or less. Even for those lucky enough to survive the worst weather events, life as we know it would cease to exist due to war, involuntary mass migration, and “catastrophic mortality events from disease, malnutrition, thirst and conflict.” According to the lead author of the report, there is no realistic plan in place to avoid this scenario.

How effective and finely tuned is this civilization-killing lie? Recently, out of curiosity, I asked the people at my nonprofit media studio, Yellow Dot, to create a graph with two data points: mentions of climate on U.S. broadcast news and recent spiking global warming numbers. And this is what they sent me:

One look at the near perfect correlatory X at the center of this graph, and it is clear something about humankind and western civilization is profoundly and deeply broken. The revelation hit me as almost biological in its clarity: as a species, we are behaving like a pod of dolphins beaching themselves because some kind of brain parasite disrupted their echolocation. Our ability to share knowledge and understand the situation we’re in has become utterly compromised, and deadly.

If so many people weren’t dying and going to die, it would almost be impressive. The lie and the financial markets, corporations, and billionaires that suckle on it have created a vast, highly sensitive information system over the decades, consisting of careerists, company men, and people who fear for their jobs. That system has so internalized big capital’s desires that it nearly instantly responds to any threat to big capital’s hegemony. And remember, by “threats” we are referring to the reality of billions of deaths.

Lately, as extreme weather goes into uncharted territory, broadcast and much of online and print news has increasingly been framing each freakish weather disaster as a one-off event disconnected from one of the fastest and most deadly shifts in Earth's history.

For example, take this clip from an NBC news report two weeks ago, about tornadoes striking New York City. It’s remarkable for how it paints a picture of the scale of the crisis we’re facing, without ever mentioning what the crisis is. And there are thousands of news pieces just like it:

Pieces like this put millions of people in active danger by robbing them of the key information they need to adjust their personal risk assessment. Namely, that because oil companies are flooding the planet with heat trapping gases, our environment is getting more and more dangerous every day.

The most recent study of the earth energy imbalance or EEI—the difference between the heat the Earth absorbs from the Sun, and the amount it sends back out into space—shows 12 Hiroshima bombs of heat being trapped by greenhouse gases every single second of every day. As recently as 2020, it was only 5 or 6 atomic bombs’ worth. That’s how fast the crisis is accelerating, but you’d never know it by watching the TV news.

It’s one thing to warn your teen daughter who is going into the city for the weekend not to take a ride from a stranger, and entirely another to fail to mention that the city she’s going to is hosting a serial killer convention.

At this exact moment, oceans are hotter than they’ve ever been since record-keeping began, and air temperatures on average are warmer than they’ve been in around 100,000 years. We refer to humans of the Pleistocene as Hunter Gatherers and not farmers, fishermen, influencers or IT consultants for a reason. Good luck taking corn to market in 135 degree Fahrenheit heat while dodging dry lightning with a saber-toothed tiger stalking you.

Back in 2015, the number chosen for preserving the Holocene and avoiding at least a billion people starving, dying in extreme heat, or in storms or fires was set at 1.5 degrees Celsius, through a mixture of science and political considerations, formalized in the Paris Climate Accord.

We are, once again for the people in the back, averaging over that number for the past three years. And never mind that several renowned scientists, like Michael Mann, think even 1.2C of warming should have been a do-not-cross line.

sentences.en: A joint study by the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries and the University of Exeter suggests that a 2C temperature increase by 2050—which we are hurtling towards, with no plans of slowing down—could result in two billion deaths.
sentences.zh: 精算师学院和埃克塞特大学的一项联合研究表明，到 2050 年，气温上升 2 摄氏度（我们正在朝着这个目标前进，而且没有放缓的计划）可能会导致 20 亿人死亡。

sentences.en: And that is virtually the best-case scenario, as temperature rise predictions have worsened and put 1.5C of warming out of reach.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是最好的情况，因为气温上升的预测已经恶化，升温 1.5 摄氏度变得遥不可及。

sentences.en: According to the United Nations, in order to limit warming to 2C, we would need “emissions to drop around 35 per cent by 2035.”
sentences.zh: 根据联合国的说法，为了将升温限制在 2 摄氏度以内，我们需要“到 2035 年排放量下降 35% 左右”。

sentences.en: Even if “current national commitments” were fully implemented they “would cut emissions only 12 to 15 per cent by that date.”
sentences.zh: 即使“当前的国家承诺”得到充分履行，“到那时也只能减少 12% 至 15% 的排放量”。

sentences.en: The other scenario, which scientists now say “recent data aligns more closely with,” is 3C of warming.
sentences.zh: 另一种情况是变暖 3 度，科学家现在表示“最近的数据更符合”。

sentences.en: At that level, the Exeter authors warn of up to 4 billion deaths.
sentences.zh: 埃克塞特大学的作者警告说，按照这个水平，将有多达 40 亿人死亡。

sentences.en: Four billion.
sentences.zh: 四十亿。

sentences.en: That is half the planet.
sentences.zh: 那是半个地球。

sentences.en: In 26 years or less.
sentences.zh: 26 年或更短的时间内。

sentences.en: Even for those lucky enough to survive the worst weather events, life as we know it would cease to exist due to war, involuntary mass migration, and “catastrophic mortality events from disease, malnutrition, thirst and conflict.”
sentences.zh: 即使对于那些幸运地在最恶劣的天气事件中幸存下来的人来说，由于战争、非自愿大规模移民以及“疾病、营养不良、口渴和冲突造成的灾难性死亡事件”，我们所知道的生命也将不复存在。

sentences.en: According to the lead author of the report, there is no realistic plan in place to avoid this scenario.
sentences.zh: 该报告的主要作者表示，目前还没有切实可行的计划来避免这种情况的发生。

sentences.en: How effective and finely tuned is this civilization-killing lie?
sentences.zh: 这个毁灭文明的谎言有多有效和巧妙？

sentences.en: Recently, out of curiosity, I asked the people at my nonprofit media studio, Yellow Dot, to create a graph with two data points: mentions of climate on U.S. broadcast news and recent spiking global warming numbers.
sentences.zh: 最近，出于好奇，我要求我的非营利媒体工作室 Yellow Dot 的人们创建一个包含两个数据点的图表：美国广播新闻中提到的气候和最近激增的全球变暖数字。

sentences.en: And this is what they sent me: One look at the near perfect correlatory X at the center of this graph, and it is clear something about humankind and western civilization is profoundly and deeply broken.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们发给我的：一看这张图中心近乎完美的相关X，很明显，人类和西方文明的某些方面已经被深刻而深刻地打破了。

sentences.en: The revelation hit me as almost biological in its clarity: as a species, we are behaving like a pod of dolphins beaching themselves because some kind of brain parasite disrupted their echolocation.
sentences.zh: 这个启示给我的启示几乎是生物学上的清晰：作为一个物种，我们的行为就像一群海豚搁浅，因为某种大脑寄生虫扰乱了它们的回声定位。

sentences.en: Our ability to share knowledge and understand the situation we’re in has become utterly compromised, and deadly.
sentences.zh: 我们分享知识和理解所处处境的能力已经完全受到损害，并且是致命的。

sentences.en: If so many people weren’t dying and going to die, it would almost be impressive.
sentences.zh: 如果这么多人没有死去或即将死去，那将是令人印象深刻的。

sentences.en: The lie and the financial markets, corporations, and billionaires that suckle on it have created a vast, highly sensitive information system over the decades, consisting of careerists, company men, and people who fear for their jobs.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，谎言以及金融市场、企业和亿万富翁创造了一个庞大的、高度敏感的信息系统，由野心家、公司职员和担心自己工作的人组成。

sentences.en: That system has so internalized big capital’s desires that it nearly instantly responds to any threat to big capital’s hegemony.
sentences.zh: 该体系已将大资本的欲望内化到几乎可以立即对大资本霸权的任何威胁做出反应。

sentences.en: And remember, by “threats” we are referring to the reality of billions of deaths.
sentences.zh: 请记住，我们所说的“威胁”指的是数十亿人死亡的现实。

sentences.en: Lately, as extreme weather goes into uncharted territory, broadcast and much of online and print news has increasingly been framing each freakish weather disaster as a one-off event disconnected from one of the fastest and most deadly shifts in Earth's history.
sentences.zh: 最近，随着极端天气进入未知领域，广播以及许多在线和印刷新闻越来越多地将每一次反常的天气灾难描述为一次性事件，与地球历史上最快和最致命的转变之一无关。

sentences.en: For example, take this clip from an NBC news report two weeks ago, about tornadoes striking New York City.
sentences.zh: 例如，取自两周前 NBC 新闻报道中的这段视频，内容是关于龙卷风袭击纽约市的。

sentences.en: It’s remarkable for how it paints a picture of the scale of the crisis we’re facing, without ever mentioning what the crisis is.
sentences.zh: 这本书的非凡之处在于它描绘了我们所面临的危机的规模，却没有提及危机是什么。

sentences.en: And there are thousands of news pieces just like it: Pieces like this put millions of people in active danger by robbing them of the key information they need to adjust their personal risk assessment.
sentences.zh: 类似的新闻报道还有数以千计：此类报道剥夺了数百万人调整个人风险评估所需的关键信息，将他们置于危险之中。

sentences.en: Namely, that because oil companies are flooding the planet with heat trapping gases, our environment is getting more and more dangerous every day.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，由于石油公司向地球注入大量吸热气体，我们的环境每天都变得越来越危险。

sentences.en: The most recent study of the earth energy imbalance or EEI—the difference between the heat the Earth absorbs from the Sun, and the amount it sends back out into space—shows 12 Hiroshima bombs of heat being trapped by greenhouse gases every single second of every day.
sentences.zh: 关于地球能量失衡（EEI）（地球从太阳吸收的热量与其发回太空的热量之间的差异）的最新研究表明，每天每一秒都有 12 枚广岛炸弹的热量被温室气体捕获。

sentences.en: As recently as 2020, it was only 5 or 6 atomic bombs’ worth.
sentences.zh: 就在2020年，它的价值还只有5、6颗原子弹。

sentences.en: That’s how fast the crisis is accelerating, but you’d never know it by watching the TV news.
sentences.zh: 这就是危机加速的速度，但你永远不会通过电视新闻知道这一点。

sentences.en: It’s one thing to warn your teen daughter who is going into the city for the weekend not to take a ride from a stranger, and entirely another to fail to mention that the city she’s going to is hosting a serial killer convention.
sentences.zh: 警告你即将进城度周末的十几岁女儿不要搭陌生人的车是一回事，而没有提及她要去的城市正在举办连环杀手大会则完全是另一回事。

sentences.en: At this exact moment, oceans are hotter than they’ve ever been since record-keeping began, and air temperatures on average are warmer than they’ve been in around 100,000 years.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，海洋温度比有记录以来的任何时候都要高，平均气温也比大约 10 万年来的最高温度要高。

sentences.en: We refer to humans of the Pleistocene as Hunter Gatherers and not farmers, fishermen, influencers or IT consultants for a reason.
sentences.zh: 我们将更新世的人类称为狩猎采集者，而不是农民、渔民、影响者或 IT 顾问，这是有原因的。

sentences.en: Good luck taking corn to market in 135 degree Fahrenheit heat while dodging dry lightning with a saber-toothed tiger stalking you.
sentences.zh: 祝您在华氏 135 度的高温下将玉米运往市场，同时躲避剑齿虎跟踪的干燥闪电，祝您好运。

sentences.en: Back in 2015, the number chosen for preserving the Holocene and avoiding at least a billion people starving, dying in extreme heat, or in storms or fires was set at 1.5 degrees Celsius, through a mixture of science and political considerations, formalized in the Paris Climate Accord.
sentences.zh: 早在 2015 年，出于科学和政治考虑，为保护全新世并避免至少 10 亿人挨饿、死于极热、暴风雨或火灾而选择的温度数字被定为 1.5 摄氏度，并在《巴黎气候协议》中正式确定。

sentences.en: We are, once again for the people in the back, averaging over that number for the past three years.
sentences.zh: 我们再次为后面的人提供了过去三年的平均数字。

sentences.en: And never mind that several renowned scientists, like Michael Mann, think even 1.2C of warming should have been a do-not-cross line.
sentences.zh: 更不用说迈克尔·曼 (Michael Mann) 等几位著名科学家认为，即使升温 1.2 摄氏度也应该是一条不可逾越的界限。

blocks.html_en: Embezzling money or murdering someone for the insurance pay-out are part of a phylum of lies that cross into serious criminality. These deceptions’ sphere of influence often stays fairly localized. But sometimes covering up the initial lie can spawn lots of other lies that spread and spread, like with Watergate or Bernie Madoff. What started as a little decorative Thanksgiving-gourd-sized lie suddenly becomes larger and quite ugly. This family of lies strives to not only avoid consequences, but to gain status and resources, another common end game of many deceptions. And then there are the large society-wide lies: hulking distortions and misrepresentations watered and tended to by leaders, mass media, culture, and industry.

blocks.html_en: Like all grand lies, “we have more time” takes many different forms, often focus-grouped. There are the lofty-sounding promises to reach “Net-zero emissions by 2050,” as if 24 years from now was soon enough. There are the queries of “What’s your carbon footprint?,” as if individual people with plastic bags or straws were the problem and not gigantic multinational corporations. There’s the accusation that anyone who expresses urgency is a “doomer.” There are those who treat climate as an abstraction to win political campaigns, first arguing that the Biden administration’s Inflation Reduction Act was a victory despite doing nowhere near enough to address the scale of climate collapse, and more recently that Democrats should just stop talking about climate and focus on more “winnable” issues. Most damaging and common of all, there are those who simply don’t mention it.

sentences.en: Like all grand lies, “we have more time” takes many different forms, often focus-grouped.
sentences.zh: 与所有宏大的谎言一样，“我们有更多的时间”有多种不同的形式，而且通常是针对焦点群体的。

sentences.en: There are the lofty-sounding promises to reach “Net-zero emissions by 2050,” as if 24 years from now was soon enough.
sentences.zh: “到 2050 年实现净零排放”的承诺听起来很崇高，就好像 24 年后就已经足够了。

sentences.en: There are the queries of “What’s your carbon footprint?,” as if individual people with plastic bags or straws were the problem and not gigantic multinational corporations.
sentences.zh: 有人问“你的碳足迹是多少？”，好像问题在于个人而不是大型跨国公司，而是拿着塑料袋或吸管的人。

sentences.en: There’s the accusation that anyone who expresses urgency is a “doomer.”
sentences.zh: 有人指责任何表达紧迫感的人都是“厄运者”。

sentences.en: There are those who treat climate as an abstraction to win political campaigns, first arguing that the Biden administration’s Inflation Reduction Act was a victory despite doing nowhere near enough to address the scale of climate collapse, and more recently that Democrats should just stop talking about climate and focus on more “winnable” issues.
sentences.zh: 有些人将气候视为赢得政治竞选的抽象概念，首先认为拜登政府的通货膨胀削减法案是一场胜利，尽管在解决气候崩溃的规模方面做得还远远不够，最近又认为民主党人应该停止谈论气候，而关注更多“可获胜”的问题。

sentences.en: Most damaging and common of all, there are those who simply don’t mention it.
sentences.zh: 最具有破坏性和最常见的是，有些人根本不提及它。

sentences.en: Let’s do the context thing again: 2C will mean we have completely left the stable climate period known as the Holocene.
sentences.zh: 让我们再回顾一下背景：2C 意味着我们已经完全离开了被称为全新世的稳定气候时期。

sentences.en: This is the 11,000-year-old era that has given us large-scale crop and livestock agriculture, which gave us cities, written language, modern science and medicine, and warm beds and showers.

blocks.html_en: Before that, for hundreds of thousands of years in the Pleistocene era, humans (and our hominid ancestors) spent most of their time running from drought, fires, floods, extreme cold and heat, predators, and each other.

sentences.en: Before that, for hundreds of thousands of years in the Pleistocene era, humans (and our hominid ancestors) spent most of their time running from drought, fires, floods, extreme cold and heat, predators, and each other.

But after the advent of the Holocene and its remarkably stable climate, in only 100 centuries the world population has risen to 8 billion.

sentences.en: The population was likely no more than a few million people spread across the whole planet.
sentences.zh: 遍布整个地球的人口可能不超过几百万。

sentences.en: At one point we may have almost gone extinct, with just 10,000 Homo sapiens clinging to life.
sentences.zh: 在某一时刻，我们可能几乎灭绝，只剩下 10,000 名智人幸存。

sentences.en: But after the advent of the Holocene and its remarkably stable climate, in only 100 centuries the world population has risen to 8 billion.
sentences.zh: 但在全新世到来及其异常稳定的气候之后，仅用了 100 个世纪，世界人口就增加到了 80 亿。

blocks.html_en: That is what we stand to lose. sentences.en: That is what we stand to lose.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们将要失去的。

sentences.en: In fact, if our institutions, news and elected officials continue to feed and water the oil company-conceived mega-falsehood that climate breakdown is something just “our great-grandkids need to worry about,” human civilization as we know it will collapse and billions could die.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果我们的机构、新闻和民选官员继续助长石油公司构想的巨大谎言，即气候崩溃只是“我们的曾孙需要担心的事情”，那么我们所知道的人类文明就会崩溃，数十亿人可能会死亡。

sentences.en: And we’re not talking about the far distant future.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是在谈论遥远的未来。

sentences.en: We are talking about collapse within years, not centuries.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是几年内而不是几个世纪内的崩溃。

sentences.en: For real.
sentences.zh: 真正的。

blocks.html_en: This is right around the corner. A joint study by the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries and the University of Exeter suggests that a 2C temperature increase by 2050—which we are hurtling towards, with no plans of slowing down—could result in two billion deaths. And that is virtually the best-case scenario, as temperature rise predictions have worsened and put 1.5C of warming out of reach. sentences.en: This is right around the corner.
sentences.zh: 这是指日可待的。

sentences.en: A joint study by the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries and the University of Exeter suggests that a 2C temperature increase by 2050—which we are hurtling towards, with no plans of slowing down—could result in two billion deaths.
sentences.zh: 精算师学院和埃克塞特大学的一项联合研究表明，到 2050 年，气温上升 2 摄氏度（我们正在朝着这个目标前进，而且没有放缓的计划）可能会导致 20 亿人死亡。

sentences.en: And that is virtually the best-case scenario, as temperature rise predictions have worsened and put 1.5C of warming out of reach.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是最好的情况，因为气温上升的预测已经恶化，升温 1.5 摄氏度变得遥不可及。

sentences.en: According to the United Nations, in order to limit warming to 2C, we would need “emissions to drop around 35 per cent by 2035.”
sentences.zh: 根据联合国的说法，为了将升温限制在 2 摄氏度以内，我们需要“到 2035 年排放量下降 35% 左右”。

sentences.en: Even if “current national commitments” were fully implemented they “would cut emissions only 12 to 15 per cent by that date.”
sentences.zh: 即使“当前的国家承诺”得到充分履行，“到那时也只能减少 12% 至 15% 的排放量”。

sentences.en: Four billion.

sentences.en: If so many people weren’t dying and going to die, it would almost be impressive.

blocks.html_en: We are, once again for the people in the back, averaging over that number for the past three years. And never mind that several renowned scientists, like Michael Mann, think even 1.2C of warming should have been a do-not-cross line.

content_html_zh:
谎言很像葫芦。 它们有数百种不同的品种、大小和球状、扭曲的形状。 有些是令人讨厌的尖刺和刺，而另一些则让我们想起秋天的童年记忆。 有些谎言，如果准备得当，比如南瓜或南瓜，可能会显得美味且不可抗拒，掩盖了一个黑暗的现实：“我不敢相信你不是模特！ 只要五千美元，我就可以给你拍照，这样你就有了一个作品集。” 大多数谎言的核心目的是避免后果。 当谎言特别绝望和自私时，它可能会无意中变得搞笑：“是的，我尝试过大麻...... 但我没有吸气。” 贪污金钱或为了保险赔偿而谋杀他人是属于严重犯罪行为的一类谎言的一部分。 这些欺骗的影响范围通常相当局部化。 但有时掩盖最初的谎言可能会催生许多其他谎言，这些谎言不断蔓延，就像水门事件或伯尼·麦道夫那样。 一开始只是一个感恩节葫芦大小的装饰性谎言突然变得更大而且相当丑陋。 这一系列谎言不仅是为了避免后果，也是为了获得地位和资源，这是许多欺骗的另一个常见的结局。 此外还有全社会范围内的大谎言：领导人、大众媒体、文化和工业所浇灌和助长的巨大歪曲和歪曲。 这种由欺骗、半真半假和战略遗漏组成的特殊亚类在整个现代历史中导致了战争、大规模死亡、社会崩溃和人类伟大宝藏被盗。 “昭昭天命。” “雅利安人的优越感。” “国王的神圣权利。” “多米诺骨牌理论。” “以色列有权保卫自己。” “奥施康定不会成瘾，因为它是延时释放的。” 这些赢得县公平、赢得蓝丝带的搪塞往往是由无数的短期激励、非理性操纵的恐惧、未经检验的假设、便利的盲点以及当然……驱动的。 避免后果并扩大地位和资源的愿望。 2007年，“人们总是支付抵押贷款”成为华尔街、新闻媒体和政界人士用来摧毁世界经济的半真半假的战斗口号。 事实证明，当你改变贷款规则，通过向无力偿还贷款的人提供抵押贷款来满足不受监管的衍生品市场的需求时…… 他们没有。 “萨达姆·侯赛因拥有大规模杀伤性武器”（以及其核心谎言的变体——“我们想要带来民主”、“如果你不支持军队，你就支持恐怖分子”、“萨达姆精心策划的9/11”等）杀死了一百万人，摧毁了整个伊拉克，并在许多方面摧毁了美国，同时让石油公司、武器制造商、大银行发财，提高电视收视率，扩大美国的权力。布什/切尼总统任期。 然而，有一种罕见的、巨大的、耸人听闻的谎言，使得人类历史上所有其他的大规模谎言看起来都像是受惊的、匆忙的、可爱的小谎言。 这是全世界数十万个机构、民选官员、许多大学、传统新闻、一些大型非营利组织所撒的谎言，最终——随着欺骗进入主流文化——甚至我们自己、对我们自己、每天的每时每刻都在撒谎。 这是一个不断生长的葫芦，在 20 世纪 70 年代还是个婴儿时，它的大小就相当于三艘航空母舰。 如今，它的规模如此之大，以至于人们更容易提及不属于它的部分（迪士尼乐园、BLT、高速公路旁的绿色鳄鱼），而不是它的一部分。 这个巨大的谎言可以最好地概括为“当谈到气候变化时...... 我们还有更多时间。” 需要明确的是，我们并不是在谈论亚历克斯·琼斯或现任美国总统等极端主义、疯狂边缘人士所发现的那种完全否认气候变化的行为。 我们指的并不是像乔·罗根或乔丹·彼得森这样的卡通小贩和“气候怀疑论者”。 民意调查显示，只有 14.8% 的美国人否认全球变暖背后的六年级基础科学。 从长远来看，多达 10% 的人仍然相信地球是平的。 不，我们所指的这个可怕的、畸形的花园巨人谎言得到了大多数美国人的认可，它已经停止和减缓了气候行动，而不仅仅是彻底否认，而且还在不断增长。 这种欺骗每天都在人类耳边诱人地低语：“全球变暖是真实的，但并不紧急...... 继续做你正在做的事情。” 这不像“气候变化是中国的骗局”那么令人尴尬，但同样不科学和荒谬，它是统治阶级、主流新闻媒体和企业最喜欢的谎言。 英国前科学顾问、牛津大学教授和剑桥大学教授、获得者太多，无法一一列举，而且这些奖项的获得者也数不胜数。有人援引戴维·金爵士的话说，我们在未来三到四年内所做的事情将决定人类的命运。 他说这... 2021年。 与所有宏大的谎言一样，“我们有更多的时间”有多种不同的形式，而且通常是针对焦点群体的。 “到 2050 年实现净零排放”的承诺听起来很崇高，就好像 24 年后就已经足够了。 有人问“你的碳足迹是多少？”，好像问题在于个人而不是大型跨国公司，而是拿着塑料袋或吸管的人。 有人指责任何表达紧迫感的人都是“厄运者”。 有些人将气候视为赢得政治竞选的抽象概念，首先认为拜登政府的通货膨胀削减法案是一场胜利，尽管在解决气候崩溃的规模方面做得还远远不够，最近又认为民主党人应该停止谈论气候，而关注更多“可获胜”的问题。 最具有破坏性和最常见的是，有些人根本不提及它。 所有这些扭曲都剥夺了人们理解威胁并相应调整行动所需的最关键要素：背景。 毫无疑问，当谈到我们有多少时间时，数据和地质记录是非常清晰的。 对于某些急需的环境而言，过去三年的平均气温超过了《巴黎协定》规定的 1.5 摄氏度，这可能是 10 万年来的首次。 仅十年前，这还被认为是灾难性的，但现在主流新闻告诉我们这只是一个数字。 明年，历史性的厄尔尼诺现象将加剧，平均气温将上升至 1.7 摄氏度，可能导致农业歉收和粮食短缺，我们正盯着吹嘘的 2C 数字。 2C为何如此被吹捧？ 让我们再回顾一下背景：2C 意味着我们已经完全离开了被称为全新世的稳定气候时期。 这是一万一千年的时代，给了我们大规模的农作物和畜牧业，给了我们城市、书面语言、现代科学和医学、温暖的床铺和淋浴。 在此之前，在更新世时代的数十万年里，人类（以及我们的原始人类祖先）大部分时间都在躲避干旱、火灾、洪水、极寒和酷热、掠食者和彼此。 遍布整个地球的人口可能不超过几百万。 在某一时刻，我们可能几乎灭绝，只剩下 10,000 名智人幸存。 但在全新世到来及其异常稳定的气候之后，仅用了 100 个世纪，世界人口就增加到了 80 亿。 这就是我们将要失去的。 事实上，如果我们的机构、新闻和民选官员继续助长石油公司构想的巨大谎言，即气候崩溃只是“我们的曾孙需要担心的事情”，那么我们所知道的人类文明就会崩溃，数十亿人可能会死亡。 我们并不是在谈论遥远的未来。 我们谈论的是几年内而不是几个世纪内的崩溃。 真正的。 这是指日可待的。 精算师学院和埃克塞特大学的一项联合研究表明，到 2050 年，气温上升 2 摄氏度（我们正在朝着这个目标前进，而且没有放缓的计划）可能会导致 20 亿人死亡。 这实际上是最好的情况，因为气温上升的预测已经恶化，升温 1.5 摄氏度变得遥不可及。 根据联合国的说法，为了将升温限制在 2 摄氏度以内，我们需要“到 2035 年排放量下降 35% 左右”。 即使“当前的国家承诺”得到充分履行，“到那时也只能减少 12% 至 15% 的排放量”。 另一种情况是变暖 3 度，科学家现在表示“最近的数据更符合”。 埃克塞特大学的作者警告说，按照这个水平，将有多达 40 亿人死亡。 四十亿。 那是半个地球。 26 年或更短的时间内。 即使对于那些幸运地在最恶劣的天气事件中幸存下来的人来说，由于战争、非自愿大规模移民以及“疾病、营养不良、口渴和冲突造成的灾难性死亡事件”，我们所知道的生命也将不复存在。 该报告的主要作者表示，目前还没有切实可行的计划来避免这种情况的发生。 这个毁灭文明的谎言有多有效和巧妙？ 最近，出于好奇，我要求我的非营利媒体工作室 Yellow Dot 的人们创建一个包含两个数据点的图表：美国广播新闻中提到的气候和最近激增的全球变暖数字。 这就是他们发给我的：一看这张图中心近乎完美的相关X，很明显，人类和西方文明的某些方面已经被深刻而深刻地打破了。 这个启示给我的启示几乎是生物学上的清晰：作为一个物种，我们的行为就像一群海豚搁浅，因为某种大脑寄生虫扰乱了它们的回声定位。 我们分享知识和理解所处处境的能力已经完全受到损害，并且是致命的。 如果这么多人没有死去或即将死去，那将是令人印象深刻的。 几十年来，谎言以及金融市场、企业和亿万富翁创造了一个庞大的、高度敏感的信息系统，由野心家、公司职员和担心自己工作的人组成。 该体系已将大资本的欲望内化到几乎可以立即对大资本霸权的任何威胁做出反应。 请记住，我们所说的“威胁”指的是数十亿人死亡的现实。 最近，随着极端天气进入未知领域，广播以及许多在线和印刷新闻越来越多地将每一次反常的天气灾难描述为一次性事件，与地球历史上最快和最致命的转变之一无关。 例如，取自两周前 NBC 新闻报道中的这段视频，内容是关于龙卷风袭击纽约市的。 这本书的非凡之处在于它描绘了我们所面临的危机的规模，却没有提及危机是什么。 类似的新闻报道还有数以千计：此类报道剥夺了数百万人调整个人风险评估所需的关键信息，将他们置于危险之中。 也就是说，由于石油公司向地球注入大量吸热气体，我们的环境每天都变得越来越危险。 关于地球能量失衡（EEI）（地球从太阳吸收的热量与其发回太空的热量之间的差异）的最新研究表明，每天每一秒都有 12 枚广岛炸弹的热量被温室气体捕获。 就在2020年，它的价值还只有5、6颗原子弹。 这就是危机加速的速度，但你永远不会通过电视新闻知道这一点。 警告你即将进城度周末的十几岁女儿不要搭陌生人的车是一回事，而没有提及她要去的城市正在举办连环杀手大会则完全是另一回事。 此时此刻，海洋温度比有记录以来的任何时候都要高，平均气温也比大约 10 万年来的最高温度要高。 我们将更新世的人类称为狩猎采集者，而不是农民、渔民、影响者或 IT 顾问，这是有原因的。 祝您在华氏 135 度的高温下将玉米运往市场，同时躲避剑齿虎跟踪的干燥闪电，祝您好运。 早在 2015 年，出于科学和政治考虑，为保护全新世并避免至少 10 亿人挨饿、死于极热、暴风雨或火灾而选择的温度数字被定为 1.5 摄氏度，并在《巴黎气候协议》中正式确定。 我们再次为后面的人提供了过去三年的平均数字。 更不用说迈克尔·曼 (Michael Mann) 等几位著名科学家认为，即使升温 1.2 摄氏度也应该是一条不可逾越的界限。

仍有疑问吗？ 如果你这样做，我不会责怪你。 我们生活在一种消费文化中，每天都会触发政治宣言、推销宣传和旨在激发大脑参与反应的点击诱饵来打击我们。 “移民是为了你的生活方式而来的！” “这款新 SUV 是有史以来最好的！” “大白鲨吃掉色情明星！” 其中大部分都以某种方式具有误导性，因此人们很自然地倾向于认为“地球即将沸腾！” 可能也是。

但石油巨头及其公关机构知道这一点，他们将我们发展起来的健康怀疑主义武器化，作为一种生存机制，反对那些说出有关气候紧急状况真相的声音。

毕竟，你会相信谁？ 《纽约时报》，一家以淡化气候紧迫性而闻名的媒体，还是某个奇怪的科学家说了疯狂的话？ 即使像保险精算师这样以冷眼旁观的底线风险评估而闻名的职业发布了一份关于情况有多严重的声明，企业新闻媒体也会将其变成人们过去所说的“幕后故事”，将其视为又一个次要的环境问题，而不是头条新闻。

为了服务于弥天大谎，英国政府甚至试图在其本国情报机构的一份气候报告泄露之前将其掩埋。 据我所知，被称为“环保人士”的间谍并不多，当然，除非他们是卧底。 但军情五处和军情六处对于即将到来的危险有着清醒的认识。 该报告警告说，“全球生态系统退化和崩溃威胁着英国的国家安全和繁荣。”

没有人想吃生南瓜。 它看起来就像苏斯博士角色的大脑，充满了种子，没有真正的味道。 但就像任何美好的谎言一样，当添加适当的糖、香料、黄油皮和烤箱的时间时，南瓜派就会成为珍贵的经典。

同样的事情也发生在气候谎言上。 金融市场、大型石油公司、为它们提供融资的银行、旅游业、汽车公司、你的职业和工作保障、与你共进晚餐的那些不想感到沮丧的人，所有这些激励和力量都不想让你知道你正在吃一个又大又奇怪的葫芦。

只要我们顺从他们的虚假潮流，在“2050 年净零排放”或“我们曾孙的未来”到来之前，数亿乃至数十亿人就会死去。 因为我们没时间了。 我们需要立即开始工作。 有一百万件事要做。
